rules.statement: Do not embed per-request state (such as requested claims) in the access token payload; carry state needed after issuance in a short-lived server-side persisted grant keyed by the token's existing `jti`, with a lifetime equal to the access token's.
rules.why: Putting it in the token makes the token bigger for every resource server and exposes what the request asked for to all of them. Persisting it keyed by `jti` leaves the token unchanged.
rules.check: Look for new claims added to the access-token payload to carry request context to later endpoints, and for persisted grants that are not keyed by `jti` or whose lifetime differs from the access token's.

rules.statement: Do not advertise or accept an optional protocol request parameter until the server actually honors it; while it is unhonored, keep its discovery flag `false` and reject requests that use it.
rules.why: Otherwise the parameter could be accepted and then silently ignored.
rules.check: Look for discovery metadata or settings flipped to `true`, or validators loosened, for a parameter whose handling is still a TODO or missing.

rules.statement: When honoring the OIDC `claims` request parameter, add the requested claims on top of the claims the scopes already imply. Treat `value`/`values` as advisory: never filter, fabricate or substitute claim values. Treat `essential` as best-effort: a missing essential claim must not fail token issuance or the UserInfo response.
rules.why: Authentication has already succeeded, and the OP returns the subject's actual claims. A host that wants stricter enforcement can register a higher-priority handler.
rules.check: Look for code that throws or returns an error when an essential claim is missing, that rewrites or invents claim values to match a requested `value`/`values`, or that replaces scope-derived claims instead of adding to them.

rules.statement: Code paths for requests that lack an optional feature (for example a request without `claims.userinfo`) must not write or read persisted state for that feature.
rules.why: The ADR requires that a request without `claims.userinfo` writes and reads nothing, so requests that don't use the feature pay no storage cost for it.
rules.check: Look for unconditional grant writes or lookups that run even when the request did not use the feature.

rules.statement: A capability setting that has a server-level ceiling must combine server, tenant and client values with `And` semantics, so a tenant or client can opt out but never enable something the server does not support.
rules.why: The server decides what it supports and advertises. Lower levels can only narrow that.
rules.check: Look for capability settings merged with override or `Or` semantics that would let a tenant or client turn on something the server has disabled.
